span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The P3b is generated by the postperceptual machinery recruited by the reporting task (categorisation, short-term memory, decision-making), not by conscious perception itself; remove the report and the component disappears even though awareness is unchanged.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Standard aware-versus-unaware contrasts confound awareness with reporting because the aware condition alone permits the extra postperceptual steps that unseen trials cannot support.

span.label: P3b → reporting
span.note: THE INDEXING / PROXY RELATION - Q-299. `from` STANDS IN FOR `to`. We have no type for it: `causes` asserts production, and `operationalised-as` says the authors CHOSE a measure, whereas a proxy claim says THIS STANDS IN FOR WHAT WE ACTUALLY CARE ABOUT AND WE KNOW IT IS NOT THE SAME THING. Measured at 8% of papers. PRESERVED BECAUSE THE EDGE IT DEFEATED WAS WITHDRAWN. `P3b --causes--> report` was retracted in Q-298 for turning a tracking relation into a causal one; without this record the paper's actual finding would have left the corpus with the bad edge. 'the P3b DOES NOT TRACK what observers are perceiving, but instead TRACKS what observers are REPORTING' - and the paper's point is that indexing report is NOT being a marker of awareness.

span.label: RETRACTED (WRONG TYPE, and the type inverts the paper's argument) · aware —operationalised-as→ no-report
span.note: RETRACTED: WRONG TYPE, and the type inverts the paper's argument. The span does not operationalise awareness AS no-report; it ARGUES that observers were aware IN the no-report condition, and gives three reasons - a longer masking interval, an incidental memory test, and the removal of masks in experiment 2. `operationalised-as` requires X to be measured as Y, and this paper's whole finding is that awareness and report DISSOCIATE ('the P3b does not track what observers are perceiving, but instead tracks what observers are reporting'), so measuring awareness as no-report would state the opposite of what it claims. WHAT THE SPAN DOES CONTAIN (Q-309): one real operationalisation, of awareness as the INCIDENTAL MEMORY TEST - 'specifically to obtain objective measures of their perceptual experience' - which is a different endpoint. No span in the staged text names both `aware` and `memory test` while asserting that relation (the two that name both state it only conditionally, or are about the P3b), so NO REPLACEMENT EDGE IS OFFERED rather than one grounded thinly. Criterion: AUDIT/edge_criterion.md - a wrong type over a correctly quoted relation is not sound; same family as the conceded Mohan2018 case, where a method that sorts things BY a variable was tagged as operationalised AS it. Found by the limitations-x-edges cross-layer queue (Q-333/334). — strength of the relation: 1 — three separate reasons are given that the stimuli were seen: a longer gap than the original study, the surprise memory test, and a whole second experiment without masks
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: prior studies always had participants report - 2026-08-26 terminal-a. THE SUBJECT OF THIS RESULT IS AN INDEFINITE STUDY, NOT THIS PAPER. `Previous studies reported`, `studies in guinea pig showed`, `recent studies have reported` - somebody else's work under a common noun rather than a name, with a citation in the sentence and no first-person marker. The quote is verbatim and the claim is true; only the attribution is wrong. FOUND BY MEASURING MY OWN CUE'S RECALL: the first sweep required a NAMED author as the subject (`Sperling (1960) demonstrated`) and found 17. Reading eleven citation-bearing findings on `Plakke2016` by hand showed four the cue could not see - `A study examining recognition found`, `studies of typical human subjects have demonstrated`, `A follow up study found` - so the named cue's 17 was a floor and not a count. A CUE'S FALSE POSITIVES TELL YOU NOTHING ABOUT ITS FALSE NEGATIVES, and the only way to find these was to read a record's whole layer. Q-1118.
